axis: politeness kept to its outward form → manners raised to excellence

members.tone: The family's floor: politeness as observed form, either done correctly or gone through with no interest at all, which is why it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.
Aims the courtesy at what another person feels rather than at a code of conduct, so it credits attention where *politeness* credits only correctness.
Measures the manner against an accepted social standard, approving conduct for meeting the rule rather than for any feeling behind it.
Defined by whom the courtesy is shown to — women — so it marks its object where *courtesy* marks only the manner.
The unmarked term for the manner itself, with no standard, object or degree attached; every word beside it adds one of those.
The same courteous regard for feelings as *respect*, but with a yielding in it — the regard shows itself by giving way.
The plainest name for conduct that respects accepted usage, so mild that the approval barely registers as praise beside *politeness*.
Not merely meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it, which puts it at the top of this family where *civility* sits at the bottom.
